surprises.description: Revenue was reported at $1.4 billion, below the preview’s $1.42–$1.44 billion consensus range, though its 12% year-over-year growth was within the preview’s expected 11%–13% range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 revenues grew 12% year-over-year to a record $1.4 billion.”

surprises.description: GAAP EPS of $0.51 was below the preview’s $0.55–$0.56 consensus, partly because of a $0.07 investment mark-to-market drag; the newly introduced adjusted EPS of $0.60 was above that range. The two measures therefore point in opposite directions versus the preview’s EPS expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP EPS was $0.51 (including a $0.07 mark-to-market drag on investments), and the newly introduced adjusted EPS was $0.60.”

surprises.description: The company said year-to-date net deposits had already surpassed its 20% annual growth target with two months left, rather than the preview’s concern that a roughly $12 billion Q3 pace could leave growth below target. October deposits exceeded $13 billion, but included a $6 billion Dell family Trump Account gift, so the reported inflow included a large one-off contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Year-to-date net deposits exceeded $68 billion, already surpassing the 20% annual growth target with two months remaining; October net deposits exceeded $13 billion including a $6 billion Dell family Trump Account gift.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Three months at $4B would be ~$12B and roughly 13% annualized — below the >20% long-term target.”

surprises.description: The full-year adjusted OpEx and SBC range was reduced to $2.675–$2.75 billion, below the preview’s $2.675–$2.775 billion range. The cut was modest, but management lowered the top end by $25 million and the midpoint by $13 million even while factoring in about $100 million of Trump Accounts investment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted OpEx and SBC guidance was lowered to $2.675–$2.75 billion, cutting the top end by $25 million and the midpoint by $13 million, with Trump Accounts representing about a $100 million full-year investment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 adj. OpEx + SBC guidance was tightened to $2.675B–$2.775B.”

surprises.description: Early Q4 event-contract average daily volumes were up about 10% from Q3, stronger than the preview’s base case of roughly flat event-contract results quarter over quarter. The preview had identified Q4 seasonality as a risk, while also noting NFL-season support.
surprises.fact_evidence: “To start Q4, average daily volumes for equities, options and crypto are tracking about 5% lighter than Q3's record levels while event contract ADVs are up about 10%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: … event contracts roughly flat q/q”; the preview also flagged “Q4 event-contract seasonality.”

surprises.description: Platform assets were nearly $400 billion, somewhat above the preview’s estimate of roughly $390 billion or more for quarter-end. Robinhood also reported Gold growth to 5 million subscribers and an 18% overall adoption rate, versus the preview’s cited Q2 baseline of 4.84 million and 17%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Platform assets reached nearly $400 billion”; “Robinhood Gold reached 5 million subscribers, up over 30% year-over-year, with an 18% overall adoption rate.”

surprises.description: Robinhood disclosed that Robinhood Chain, launched July 1, had become a top-five chain and generated over $100 billion in DEX volume and about $50 million in gross chain fees (roughly $25 million net) in its first quarter. The preview did not anticipate or quantify this new activity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Robinhood Chain launched July 1 and became a top-5 chain, generating over $100 billion in DEX volume and roughly $50 million in gross chain fees (~$25 million net) in its first quarter.”

surprises.description: The company said it now has 14 revenue “cylinders” each generating at least $100 million in annualized revenue, a breadth and scale of revenue sources the preview did not identify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company now has 14 revenue 'cylinders' each generating $100 million or more in annualized revenue.”

surprises.description: Robinhood disclosed new crypto.com and og.com partnerships that give it an initial 1% equity stake in each without cash outlay, with potential ownership of up to 10%, and make them the primary secondary prediction-market exchange behind Rothera. The preview discussed Rothera and multi-venue strategy but did not anticipate these partnerships or their equity terms.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The crypto.com and og.com partnerships gave Robinhood an initial 1% equity stake in each with no cash outlay and potential to reach up to 10% ownership, establishing them as the primary secondary prediction market exchange behind Rothera.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed “Rothera economics and multi-venue strategy (Kalshi/ForecastEx retained).”
